relevance_note: The paper describes an individual ALDH5A1-variant patient and relatives: 'the patient was found to be heterozygous for two missense variants in the ALDH5A1 gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values I chose. The paper is a functional study of one SSADH-D family: the index patient (label 'patient', rule 5; 'index patient' is a role word), his mother (healthy carrier) and his younger sister (heterozygous carrier). The father is never described as a person: the paper only calls Cys93Phe the 'paternal variant' and says 'The parents provided a signed informed consent', so he gets no row; the patient's Cys93Phe is recorded as inherited paternal from that attribution. His180Tyr (c.538T>C, rs2760118, allelic frequency 0.348) is a common SNP the authors call benign/not pathogenic per se, so per the v4 rule it gets no variant row; it lies in cis with Asn255Asp on the maternal allele (patient and mother), which is noted in the Asn255Asp rows. Val90Ala is not described as common and was a VUS shown to be non-pathogenic; it is kept for the mother and sister. Variant type 'missense' for mother and sister rows comes from Methods 4.3, which names these exact variants as 'SSADH missense variants'. Patient zygosity 'compound heterozygous' combines 'heterozygous for two missense variants' with the Figure 1 legend; mother's zygosity is not stated ('healthy carrier'), so not reported. Functional and pathogenicity statements are about these exact variants (cell-line assays and patient fibroblasts). The fibroblast drug treatments (arimoclomol, betaine, celastrol) were in vitro only, not given to the patient, so treatment_summary is not reported. The acknowledgment of 'Nana, who passed away' refers to an author (Tiegel Nana), not the patient. Contradictions in the paper: (1) Methods 4.1 gives 'c.278G>T, p.Cys93Phe' while Results and Figure 1 give 'c.278C>T'; the Results/Figure form is recorded. (2) Methods 4.1 places '(paternal)' after 'c.538T>C' (His180Tyr), while Results/Figure 1 say Cys93Phe is paternal and His180Tyr is on the maternal allele. (3) The Introduction once writes 'Asn255Ala' where everywhere else the variant is Asn255Asp. (4) The Figure 1 legend says all four variants were 'present in a compound heterozygous form' although Val90Ala was not found in the patient. No transcript is given for the variants (NM_001080.3 appears only for gRNA design) so transcript is not reported. No stacked cells; no tables with patients.
